1.1: There was this man from Ramathaim, up in the hill country of Ephraim. His name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, grandson of Elihu, great-grandson of Tohu, from the family of Zuph. He was an Ephraimite.
1.2: Elkanah had two wives—one named Hannah, the other named Peninnah. Peninnah had kids, but Hannah ain't have none.
1.3: Every year, Elkanah took his whole family up to Shiloh to worship and bring sacrifices to the Lord Almighty. Now, Eli's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, was working as priests for the Lord at that time.
1.4: Whenever Elkanah made his offering, he would give Peninnah and all her kids their share.
1.5: But when it came to Hannah, he gave her extra 'cause he really loved her, even though the Lord ain't blessed her with no kids.
1.6: But Peninnah? She stayed clownin' Hannah, making her feel real bad 'cause she ain't have no kids.
1.7: This went down every single year when they went up to the Lord's house. Peninnah kept coming at her, making Hannah cry so much she ain't even wanna eat.
1.8: Elkanah, her husband, was like, 'Hannah, why you cryin'? Why you ain't eatin'? Why your heart so heavy? Ain't I better to you than ten sons?'
1.9: One time after they finished eating in Shiloh, Hannah got up. Meanwhile, Eli the priest was chillin' by the entrance of the Lord's temple.
1.10: Hannah was hurting deep in her soul. She started praying hard to the Lord, crying her heart out.
1.11: She made a promise and said, 'Lord Almighty, if you see my struggle, if you remember me and bless me with a son, I promise to give him back to you for his whole life. And no razor gon' touch his head.'
1.12: She kept prayin' for a long time, and Eli was just sittin' there watchin' her mouth move.
1.13: Hannah was prayin' in her heart—her lips was movin', but she ain't say nothin' out loud. So Eli thought she was drunk.
1.14: Eli was like, 'How long you gon' be drunk? Put that wine down!'
1.15: But Hannah said, 'No sir, I ain't drunk. I'm just a woman with a heavy heart, and I been pourin' my soul out to the Lord.'
1.16: 'Please don't think I'm some kinda worthless woman. I been speakin' out of deep pain and frustration.'
1.17: Eli answered, 'Alright then, go in peace. And may the God of Israel give you what you been askin' for.'
1.18: Hannah said, 'Thank you for your kindness!' Then she went back, got herself some food, and wasn't sad no more.
1.19: Early the next morning, Elkanah and his family worshiped the Lord, then headed back home to Ramah. Elkanah slept with Hannah, and the Lord remembered her.
1.20: After some time, Hannah got pregnant and had a son. She named him Samuel, sayin', 'Because I asked the Lord for him.'
1.21: Elkanah went up with his whole household to give their yearly sacrifice and fulfill his vow.
1.22: But Hannah ain't go. She told her husband, 'Let me wait till the child is weaned. Then I'll take him to the Lord's house, and he gon' stay there forever.'
1.23: Elkanah said, 'Do what you think is best. Stay here till you wean him, but let the Lord's will be done.' So Hannah stayed home and nursed her son.
1.24: When she finished weaning him, she took him to the Lord's house in Shiloh. She brought a three-year-old bull, a bunch of flour, and a skin of wine. The boy was still real young.
1.25: They sacrificed the bull and brought Samuel to Eli.
1.26: Hannah told Eli, 'Sir, I swear I'm that woman that was standin' here prayin' to the Lord.'
1.27: 'I was prayin' for this child, and the Lord gave me what I asked for.'
1.28: 'So now I'm givin' him back to the Lord. As long as he live, he belong to the Lord.' And they worshiped the Lord there.

2.1: Then Hannah prayed and said: 'My heart is full of joy in the Lord. He lifted me up! I can laugh in the face of my enemies 'cause I know the Lord saved me.'
2.2: 'Ain't nobody holy like the Lord. Ain't nobody else like Him, and ain't no rock as solid as our God.'
2.3: 'Y'all need to stop talkin' all high and mighty. Quit all that arrogance, 'cause the Lord sees everything and He weighs every action.'
2.4: 'The weapons of the strong are broken, but the ones who was strugglin' now got strength.'
2.5: 'The ones who had everything gotta work just to eat, but the hungry? They full now. The woman who couldn't have kids got seven, but the one with many kids is weak now.'
2.6: 'The Lord brings life, and He takes it away. He puts folks in the grave, and He lifts them up.'
2.7: 'The Lord makes some folks poor and others rich. He humbles some and lifts others up.'
2.8: 'He takes the poor up out the dirt, pulls the beggar up out the ashes, and sets 'em up with princes, giving them a seat at the table. The whole world rests on His foundation.'
2.9: 'The Lord keeps His people safe, but the wicked? They get left in the dark. 'Cause ain't no man can win just by his own strength.'
2.10: 'The Lord gon' shatter His enemies. When He speaks from heaven, they gon' be done for. He judges everybody, from one end of the earth to the other. He gon' give power to His king and lift up the one He chose.'
2.11: After that, Elkanah took his family back home to Ramah, but little Samuel stayed and served the Lord under Eli the priest.
2.12: Now Eli's sons? They was outta pocket. They ain't know the Lord at all.
2.13: Back in the day, priests had this routine—when people brought sacrifices, the priest's servant would come through while the meat was still boiling, holding a three-pronged fork.
2.14: He'd stick the fork into the pot or kettle, and whatever came up, the priest took for himself. That's how they did all the Israelites bringing sacrifices in Shiloh.
2.15: But before the fat was even burned, the priest's servant would tell the person sacrificing, 'Yo, hand over that raw meat for the priest to roast. He ain't takin' no boiled meat—only raw.'
2.16: If somebody said, 'Nah, they gotta burn the fat first, then you can take what you want,' the servant would snap back, 'Nope, gimme that now, or I'll take it by force!'
2.17: These young priests was outta control, and the Lord was not pleased. They was making folks hate bringing offerings to the Lord.
2.18: Meanwhile, little Samuel was servin' the Lord, rockin' his linen priest's robe.
2.19: His mama, Hannah, made him a little coat and brought it to him every year when they came up to offer sacrifices.
2.20: Eli would bless Elkanah and Hannah, saying, 'May the Lord give y'all more kids 'cause of the one you gave back to Him.' Then they'd go back home.
2.21: And the Lord blessed Hannah. She had three more sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, little Samuel was growin' up right in front of the Lord.
2.22: Now Eli was old. He kept hearing 'bout all the shady stuff his sons was doin'—how they was messin' with the women who worked at the entrance of the Lord's tent.
2.23: So he told 'em, 'Why y'all actin' like this? Everybody out here talkin' 'bout how y'all wildin' out.'
2.24: 'This ain't a good look, my sons. Y'all makin' God's people sin! This ain't right.'
2.25: 'If a man sins against another man, God can step in. But if a man sins against the Lord, who gon' step in for him?' But they ain't listen to their daddy, 'cause the Lord had already decided their fate.
2.26: Meanwhile, Samuel kept growin' in stature and was favored by both God and people.
2.27: Then one day, a man of God came to Eli and said, 'This what the Lord says: Didn't I reveal myself to your ancestors back when they was slaves in Egypt?'
2.28: 'Didn't I choose your family to be My priests, to serve at My altar, burn incense, and wear the sacred robe before Me? Didn't I give your family all the sacrifices made by fire?'
2.29: 'So why y'all disrespectin' My offerings? Why you let your sons treat My sacrifices like trash? You put them above Me, getting fat off the best of the offerings.'
2.30: 'So now the Lord, the God of Israel, says this: I did say your family would serve Me forever. But nah, I don't roll like that. If you honor Me, I'll honor you. But if you despise Me, you gon' be ignored.'
2.31: 'Days are coming when I'ma cut off your family line. None of y'all gon' grow old.'
2.32: 'You gon' see disaster in My house. And while Israel gets blessed, y'all gon' be struggling. Your whole family gon' be wiped out.'
2.33: 'I'ma leave one of your descendants alive, but he gon' be struggling, breaking your heart. And the rest of 'em? They gon' die young.'
2.34: 'And this how you know it's real—your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas? They both gon' die on the same day.'
2.35: 'But I'ma raise up a real priest, somebody who follows My heart and does what I want. I'ma make sure his house stands strong, and he gon' serve My anointed one forever.'
2.36: 'And when that happens, anybody left from your family gon' be begging for food, sayin', "Please let me work for you, so I can get a bite to eat."'

3.1: Lil' Samuel was servin' the Lord under Eli. Now back then, the Lord ain't be speakin' much—visions and messages from God was real rare.
3.2: One night, Eli was layin' down in his spot. His eyesight was bad, like real bad—man could barely see no more.
3.3: Samuel was layin' down in the Lord's temple, right where the Ark of God was. The lamp of God was still burnin'.
3.4: Then the Lord called out, 'Samuel!' And Samuel jumped up like, 'Here I am!'
3.5: He ran straight to Eli like, 'I'm here! You called me?' But Eli was like, 'Nah, boy, I ain't call you. Go lay back down.' So Samuel went back to bed.
3.6: Then the Lord called out again, 'Samuel!' So Samuel got up, ran to Eli again, and said, 'I'm here! You called me?' But Eli was like, 'Son, I did not call you. Go lay down.'
3.7: Now Samuel ain't really know the Lord yet, 'cause God ain't spoke to him before.
3.8: Then the Lord called Samuel one more time. Samuel jumped up, ran to Eli, and said, 'I know you called me!' That's when Eli finally realized—oh, this God talkin' to the boy.
3.9: So Eli told him, 'Go lay down again. And if you hear that voice, say, "Speak, Lord, your servant is listenin'."' So Samuel went back to his bed.
3.10: Then the Lord showed up and called just like before, 'Samuel! Samuel!' And Samuel said, 'Speak, Lord. I'm listenin'.'
3.11: Then the Lord said, 'Boy, listen—I'm 'bout to do somethin' in Israel that gon' have everybody's ears ringin'.'
3.12: 'When the time come, I'ma do everything I said I was gon' do to Eli's family—ain't nothin' gettin' left out.'
3.13: 'I already told Eli his family gettin' judged forever, 'cause his sons out here actin' a fool, and he ain't stop 'em.'
3.14: 'Ain't no amount of sacrifices or offerings ever gon' fix this. It's done.'
3.15: Samuel laid there till morning, then got up and opened the temple doors. But he did not wanna tell Eli what he heard.
3.16: Eli called him, 'Samuel, my son!' And Samuel was like, 'I'm here.'
3.17: Eli said, 'What the Lord tell you? Don't you hide nothin' from me. If you do, may God do the same and worse to you!'
3.18: So Samuel told him everything—ain't hold nothin' back. Eli sighed and said, 'Well, it's the Lord. He gon' do what He think is best.'
3.19: Samuel grew up, and the Lord was with him. Everything Samuel spoke? It came true.
3.20: From Dan to Beersheba, everybody in Israel knew Samuel was the Lord's prophet.
3.21: The Lord kept showin' up in Shiloh, speakin' to Samuel and makin' Himself known.

4.1: Samuel's word was spreadin' all over Israel. Meanwhile, Israel's army rolled out to fight the Philistines, settin' up camp at Ebenezer while the Philistines posted up at Aphek.
4.2: When the battle popped off, the Philistines straight-up whooped Israel. They took out about 4,000 soldiers out on the battlefield.
4.3: After takin' that L, the Israelite elders was like, 'Man, why did the Lord let us lose like this? We need to bring the Ark of the Covenant from Shiloh—that gon' help us win!'
4.4: So they sent folks to Shiloh to grab the Ark of the Lord's Covenant, the one that sits between the cherubim. Eli's two shady sons, Hophni and Phinehas, came along with it.
4.5: When the Ark pulled up in the camp, all of Israel went wild—yellin' so loud the ground was shakin'!
4.6: The Philistines heard the ruckus and was like, 'Hold up—what's all that shoutin' about in the Hebrew camp?' Then they realized, 'Oh snap, the Ark of the Lord just pulled up.'
4.7: They got shook. 'Oh no! Their God just showed up in the camp! We ain't never seen nothin' like this before!'
4.8: 'We in trouble now! This the same God that wrecked Egypt with all them plagues!'
4.9: 'Man up, Philistines! If y'all don't fight, y'all gon' end up slaves to these Hebrews just like they been to us. Get it together and fight!'
4.10: And fight they did—and Israel lost bad. Every man ran back home. 30,000 soldiers got wiped out.
4.11: And worst of all? The Ark of God got snatched up. Hophni and Phinehas? Dead.
4.12: Same day, a dude from the tribe of Benjamin sprinted back from the battlefield straight to Shiloh. His clothes was torn, dirt all over his head—he was tore up.
4.13: When he got there, Eli was sittin' by the road, watchin'—his heart was racin' 'cause he was worried about the Ark. Soon as the runner hit town and told the people what happened, the whole city started cryin' out.
4.14: Eli heard the noise and was like, 'What's goin' on?!' The runner rushed over and told him everything.
4.15: Now Eli was 98 years old and practically blind.
4.16: The runner said, 'I just came from the battlefield—I had to run back here today.' Eli asked, 'What happened, son?'
4.17: The man broke it down: 'Israel got washed by the Philistines, it was a massacre. Your two sons? Hophni and Phinehas? They gone. And on top of that, the Ark of God got taken.'
4.18: Soon as he heard about the Ark, Eli fell backward off his seat, snapped his neck, and died—man was old and heavy. He had been judge over Israel for 40 years.
4.19: Meanwhile, Phinehas' wife was pregnant and just about due. Soon as she heard the news—that the Ark was taken, that her father-in-law and her husband was dead—she went into labor right then and there.
4.20: As she was dyin' in labor, the women helpin' her was like, 'Don't worry, you had a son!' But she ain't even respond.
4.21: She named the baby Ichabod and said, 'The glory is gone from Israel!' 'Cause the Ark was taken, and her husband and father-in-law was gone.
4.22: 'Yeah, the glory done left Israel, 'cause the Ark of God got taken.'

5.1: The Philistines took the Ark of God from Ebenezer and hauled it off to Ashdod.
5.2: They brought it into the temple of Dagon, their so-called god, and set it up right next to the statue.
5.3: But when the folks in Ashdod woke up the next morning, Dagon was laid out flat, face-down in front of the Ark of the Lord. So they picked him up and put him back where he was.
5.4: Next morning? Same thing—except this time, Dagon's head and both hands was broken clean off at the threshold. Only thing left standing was his torso.
5.5: That's why to this day, Dagon's priests and his worshippers won't step on that threshold in Ashdod—'cause they know what happened.
5.6: But the Lord wasn't done yet. He put heavy pressure on Ashdod—struck 'em down with nasty tumors all over the city and surrounding areas.
5.7: Folks in Ashdod started freakin' out: 'We gotta get rid of this Ark, 'cause God's hand is straight-up destroyin' us and makin' our god, Dagon, look weak!'
5.8: So they gathered up all the big bosses of the Philistines and asked, 'What we gon' do with this Ark?' They decided, 'Send it to Gath.' So they moved it there.
5.9: But soon as it got to Gath, God went off again—the whole city got hit hard, from the rich folks down to the common folk. Tumors broke out everywhere.
5.10: So they panicked and sent the Ark to Ekron. But soon as it pulled up, the Ekronites flipped out: 'Y'all brought the Ark here to kill us all?!'
5.11: So once again, the Philistine leaders had a meeting and decided, 'Man, get this thing outta here! Send it back to Israel before it wipes us all out!' The whole city was gettin' wrecked, and God's hand was pressin' down hard on 'em.
5.12: Some folks straight-up died, while others was suffering from tumors. The whole city was cryin' out for mercy—their screams went straight up to heaven.

6.1: The Ark of the Lord had been stuck in Philistine territory for seven months.
6.2: The Philistines called in their priests and fortune tellers like, 'Yo, what we supposed to do with this Ark? How we send it back?'
6.3: They told 'em, 'Look, if y'all gon' send the Ark back, don't send it empty-handed. Make sure you bring an offering for the Lord. Maybe then He'll heal y'all and stop messin' y'all up.'
6.4: So they asked, 'Aight, but what kinda offering we supposed to give?' They answered, 'Five golden tumors and five golden rats—one for each Philistine leader, 'cause all y'all got hit by the same plague.'
6.5: 'Make models of the tumors and rats messin' up y'all land, and send 'em as a peace offering to the God of Israel. Maybe He'll chill out and stop wreckin' y'all, your gods, and your land.'
6.6: 'Don't be stubborn like Pharaoh and the Egyptians! Y'all remember what happened to them, right? God showed out, and they had no choice but to let Israel go!'
6.7: 'Now here's what y'all do—get a new cart, take two cows that ain't never been yoked before, and hitch 'em up. Take their calves and keep 'em at home.'
6.8: 'Put the Ark of the Lord on the cart, and put y'all gold offerings in a box next to it. Then let it go, and see what happens.'
6.9: 'If the cows head straight for Beth Shemesh, then we'll know it was the Lord who was punishin' us. But if they don't, then it was all just bad luck.'
6.10: So they did just that—hitched up the two cows, locked up their calves, and sent the Ark on its way.
6.11: They put the Ark of the Lord on the cart, along with the box of golden rats and tumors.
6.12: The cows walked straight down the road to Beth Shemesh, mooin' the whole way. They ain't turn left or right. The Philistine leaders followed behind, watchin' to see what would happen.
6.13: The folks in Beth Shemesh was out in the fields harvesting wheat when they looked up and saw the Ark comin'. They got hype!
6.14: The cart rolled into a field belongin' to a man named Joshua and stopped by a big rock. The Israelites chopped up the wood from the cart and sacrificed the cows as an offering to the Lord.
6.15: The Levites took down the Ark and the gold offerings and set them up on the rock. That day, the people of Beth Shemesh gave offerings and sacrifices to the Lord.
6.16: When the five Philistine leaders saw all this go down, they was like, 'Aight, bet.' And they headed back to Ekron.
6.17: Them golden tumors the Philistines sent as a guilt offering to the Lord? One for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
6.18: Same with the golden rats—one for every city in Philistine territory, whether big or small. They placed the Ark on a rock in Joshua's field in Beth Shemesh, and that rock still there to this day.
6.19: But some men in Beth Shemesh got curious and peeked inside the Ark. Big mistake. The Lord struck 50,070 of them dead. The people started mournin', 'cause they knew the Lord wasn't playin'.
6.20: They was like, 'Man, who can even stand before the Lord? He too holy! Where we gon' send the Ark now?!'
6.21: So they sent a message to the folks in Kirjath Jearim: 'Yo, the Philistines sent the Ark back. Y'all come get it!'

7.1: So the men of Kirjath Jearim came and took the Ark of the Lord. They brought it to Abinadab's house up on the hill and put his son Eleazar in charge of watching over it.
7.2: That Ark stayed in Kirjath Jearim for twenty years. And in all that time, Israel was cryin' out to the Lord, wantin' to get right with Him.
7.3: Samuel told the whole nation of Israel, 'If y'all really wanna come back to the Lord, then drop them fake gods—get rid of all them idols, especially the Ashtoreths. Y'all need to commit to servin' the Lord only, and He'll save you from the Philistines.'
7.4: So Israel did just that—they threw away their idols to Baal and Ashtoreth, and they only served the Lord.
7.5: Then Samuel said, 'Aight, everybody, meet me at Mizpah. I'ma pray to the Lord for y'all.'
7.6: So they gathered up at Mizpah, poured out water as an offering to God, and fasted that whole day. They admitted, 'Lord, we messed up. We sinned against You.' That day, Samuel acted as their judge.
7.7: When the Philistines heard Israel was all gathered up at Mizpah, their leaders was like, 'Oh, they slippin'—let's go get 'em.' Israel heard the Philistines was comin' and got scared.
7.8: They begged Samuel, 'Please, don't stop prayin' to the Lord for us! Ask Him to save us from the Philistines!'
7.9: So Samuel took a baby lamb and sacrificed it as a burnt offering to the Lord. He cried out to the Lord for Israel, and God answered him.
7.10: Just as Samuel was makin' the sacrifice, the Philistines rolled up ready for war. But the Lord let out a massive thunderclap so loud that it shook the Philistines, throwin' 'em into complete chaos. Israel took 'em down.
7.11: The Israelites chased the Philistines all the way back to Beth Car, tearin' 'em up along the way.
7.12: After the battle, Samuel took a big stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, sayin', 'This far, the Lord has helped us.'
7.13: From that day on, the Philistines stayed down—they ain't dare mess with Israel no more. The Lord kept His hand against them the whole time Samuel was alive.
7.14: Any cities the Philistines had taken got returned to Israel, from Ekron to Gath. Israel also made peace with the Amorites.
7.15: Samuel led and judged Israel for the rest of his life.
7.16: Every year, he made the rounds from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging the people in each city.
7.17: But his home base was Ramah, where he also judged Israel. He even built an altar to the Lord there.

8.1: When Samuel got old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
8.2: His firstborn was named Joel, and his second son was Abijah. They was posted up in Beersheba, judging the people.
8.3: But these dudes? They ain't walk like Samuel. They got greedy, takin' bribes, messin' up justice for personal gain.
8.4: So all the elders of Israel pulled up on Samuel at Ramah.
8.5: They told him, 'Look, man, you old now, and your sons ain't doin' right. We need you to give us a king—somebody to rule over us like all the other nations.'
8.6: Samuel ain't like that at all. He took it straight to the Lord in prayer.
8.7: The Lord told Samuel, 'Listen to 'em. They ain't rejecting you, they rejecting Me—they don't want Me running things no more.'
8.8: 'Ain't nothin' new. Ever since I brought 'em outta Egypt, they been turnin' away from Me, runnin' after fake gods. And now they doin' the same thing to you.'
8.9: 'Go ahead and give 'em what they want, but make sure you tell 'em what a king really gon' do to 'em.'
8.10: So Samuel sat the people down and gave them the real about kings.
8.11: He said, 'This what a king gon' be like—he gon' snatch up your sons, make 'em run his chariots, ride his horses, and serve in his army.'
8.12: 'He gon' put some of y'all in charge of thousands, some over fifties, and some just to work his farms and make his weapons.'
8.13: 'He gon' take your daughters to be his perfumers, cooks, and bakers.'
8.14: 'He gon' snatch up the best of your fields, vineyards, and olive groves, and hand 'em over to his own people.'
8.15: 'He gon' tax your grain and grapes, takin' a cut for himself and his staff.'
8.16: 'Your servants, your best workers, your livestock—he gon' put 'em all to work for him.'
8.17: 'He gon' take a tenth of your sheep, and at the end of the day? Y'all gon' be his servants.'
8.18: 'And when that day come, when y'all realize y'all messed up and cry out to the Lord about the king y'all chose? He ain't gon' listen.'
8.19: But the people ain't wanna hear all that. They said, 'Nah! We need a king!'
8.20: 'We wanna be like everybody else, with a king who can lead us and fight our battles!'
8.21: Samuel listened to all their demands, then went back and told the Lord.
8.22: And the Lord said, 'Fine. Give 'em a king.' Then Samuel told the people, 'Aight, everybody go home.'

9.1: There was a man from the tribe of Benjamin named Kish, son of Abiel, grandson of Zeror, great-grandson of Bechorath, from the family of Aphiah. Dude was powerful.
9.2: Kish had a son named Saul, and let me tell you—this man was fine. Nobody in Israel looked better than him. Plus, he was tall, standing a whole head above everybody else.
9.3: One day, Kish's donkeys went missing, so he told Saul, 'Take one of the servants and go look for them.'
9.4: Saul and his servant searched all over—through the Ephraim hills, through Shalisha, through Shaalim, and even through Benjamin's land—but no donkeys.
9.5: When they got to Zuph, Saul told his servant, 'Man, let's go back. My dad gon' stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.'
9.6: But the servant was like, 'Hold up—there's a man of God in this city. Everything he says comes true. Maybe he can tell us where to look.'
9.7: Saul was like, 'Aight, but what we gon' give him? We outta food, and we ain't got no gift for the man of God. What we got left?'
9.8: The servant said, 'I got a fourth of a shekel of silver. I'll give it to the man of God so he can tell us where to go.'
9.9: (Back in the day, people used to call prophets seers. If you wanted to hear from God, you'd say, 'Let's go see the seer.')
9.10: Saul was like, 'Bet, let's go.' So they headed into the city to find the man of God.
9.11: As they climbed the hill toward the city, they saw some young women comin' out to draw water. They asked, 'Hey, is the seer around?'
9.12: The women said, 'Yeah, he's up ahead! But y'all better hurry, 'cause he just got here for a big sacrifice at the high place.'
9.13: 'If y'all go now, you'll catch him before he goes up to bless the sacrifice. The people won't eat till he gets there. Go quick, you'll find him!'
9.14: So they went into the city, and boom—Samuel was walking right toward them on his way up to the high place.
9.15: Now, the day before, the Lord had whispered to Samuel,
9.16: 'Tomorrow, around this time, I'ma send you a man from Benjamin. You gon' anoint him as leader over My people Israel. He gon' rescue them from the Philistines, 'cause I heard their cries.'
9.17: When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said, 'That's him! The one I told you about—he gon' rule over My people.'
9.18: Saul walked up to Samuel at the city gate and said, 'Excuse me, sir—can you tell me where the seer's house is?'
9.19: Samuel said, 'That's me. Come with me up to the high place. You gon' eat with me today, and tomorrow morning, I'ma tell you everything on your heart.'
9.20: 'Oh, and about them donkeys y'all been lookin' for? Don't even worry 'bout it. They been found. But let me ask you this—who do you think all of Israel lookin' to now? Ain't it you and your family?'
9.21: Saul was shocked. 'Me? But I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel! And my family? We ain't nobody special. Why you talkin' to me like this?'
9.22: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining hall and gave them the best seat at the table with about thirty guests.
9.23: Then Samuel told the cook, 'Bring out that special piece I set aside for our guest.'
9.24: So the cook brought out the thigh and the best cut and placed it in front of Saul. Samuel said, 'This was saved just for you. Go ahead, eat!' So Saul sat and ate with Samuel that day.
9.25: After dinner, they came back down from the high place into the city. Samuel had a private talk with Saul up on the rooftop.
9.26: The next morning, at sunrise, Samuel called to Saul, 'Wake up! It's time for you to go.' So Saul got up, and they walked out together.
9.27: As they were leavin' the city, Samuel told Saul, 'Send your servant ahead of us.' When the servant left, Samuel said, 'Now, stay here for a minute—I gotta tell you what God has planned for you.'

10.1: Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul's head, kissed him, and said, 'The Lord just anointed you as the leader over His people.'
10.2: 'When you leave me today, you gon' run into two men near Rachel's tomb in Benjamin, at Zelzah. They gon' tell you, "Yo, them donkeys you was lookin' for? They been found. But now your pops ain't even worried about them—he worried about you instead."'
10.3: 'Then, when you keep going to the great tree at Tabor, you gon' run into three men on their way to worship in Bethel. One got three goats, one got three loaves of bread, and one got a skin of wine.'
10.4: 'They gon' greet you and hand you two loaves of bread. Take it—it's yours.'
10.5: 'Then you gon' reach Gibeah, where the Philistine outpost is. There, you gon' run into some prophets comin' down from the high place, playing instruments—harps, tambourines, flutes—and they gon' be prophesyin'.'
10.6: 'When that happens, the Spirit of the Lord gon' take over you, and you gon' start prophesyin' too. You gon' be a whole new man.'
10.7: 'When all this goes down, do whatever feels right, 'cause God is with you.'
10.8: 'Then go ahead to Gilgal, and I'ma come later to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings. Wait seven days for me to get there and tell you what's next.'
10.9: Soon as Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed his heart. And just like that, everything Samuel said started happening.
10.10: When Saul and his servant got to the hill, there was a group of prophets. And just like that, the Spirit of God hit Saul, and he started prophesyin' too.
10.11: Everybody who knew Saul before was shocked. They was like, 'Wait… what's goin' on with Kish's son?! Saul's a prophet now?!'
10.12: One dude was like, 'Who even taught these prophets?!' And that's how the saying started: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
10.13: When Saul finished prophesyin', he went up to the high place.
10.14: Later, Saul's uncle asked him and his servant, 'Where y'all been?' Saul said, 'Lookin' for the donkeys. When we couldn't find 'em, we went to see Samuel.'
10.15: His uncle was like, 'What did Samuel tell y'all?'
10.16: Saul said, 'Oh, he just told us the donkeys was found.' But he ain't say a word about Samuel anointing him as king.
10.17: Samuel called all the people together at Mizpah to meet with the Lord.
10.18: He told them, 'The Lord, the God of Israel, says: I brought y'all out of Egypt. I saved y'all from slavery and from every nation that oppressed y'all.'
10.19: 'But today, y'all rejecting God—the same God who keeps saving you. Y'all said, "Nah, we want a king instead!" So now, line up by tribes and clans so we can pick one.'
10.20: Samuel had all the tribes line up, and the Lord picked the tribe of Benjamin.
10.21: Then He picked the Matri clan from Benjamin. Then, from them, He picked Saul, son of Kish. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
10.22: So they asked the Lord, 'Uh… where he at?' And the Lord said, 'He hidin' in the baggage.'
10.23: So they ran and pulled Saul out. And when he stood up, he was taller than everybody else.
10.24: Samuel said, 'Look at him—this is the one God chose! Ain't nobody like him in all of Israel!' And the people went crazy, shoutin', 'Long live the king!'
10.25: Then Samuel explained how the kingdom was supposed to run, wrote it all down in a book, and placed it before the Lord. Then he sent everybody home.
10.26: Saul went back to Gibeah, and some loyal men followed him—men whose hearts God had touched.
10.27: But some haters was like, 'Man, how he supposed to save us?' They disrespected him, ain't bring him no gifts. But Saul? He ain't say nothin'.

11.1: Then Nahash the Ammonite rolled up on Jabesh Gilead, ready to take over. The men of Jabesh was like, 'Aight, let's make a deal—we'll serve you if you let us live.'
11.2: Nahash was like, 'Bet. But on one condition—I'ma gouge out all y'all right eyes to humiliate Israel.'
11.3: The elders of Jabesh was like, 'Hold up! Give us seven days to send out messengers across Israel. If nobody comes to save us, then we'll surrender.'
11.4: So they sent messengers to Gibeah, where Saul was. When the people heard what was goin' down, they all started cryin'.
11.5: Meanwhile, Saul was out in the field workin'. When he came back, he saw everybody weepin' and was like, 'What's goin' on?' So they told him what happened with Jabesh.
11.6: Soon as Saul heard the news, the Spirit of God hit him hard, and he got mad as hell.
11.7: Saul took two oxen, chopped 'em up, and sent the pieces across Israel with a message: 'Anybody who don't come fight with me and Samuel? This what gon' happen to their oxen too!' The Lord put fear in the people, so they all showed up ready to fight.
11.8: When Saul did a headcount at Bezek, he had 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men from Judah.
11.9: They sent a message back to Jabesh Gilead, sayin', 'Tell your people that by noon tomorrow, help is comin'.' When Jabesh heard that, they got hype.
11.10: So the men of Jabesh told Nahash, 'Aight, we comin' out tomorrow—do whatever you want to us.' (But little did Nahash know, help was already on the way.)
11.11: Next morning, Saul split his army into three groups. They attacked the Ammonite camp before sunrise and kept slaughterin' 'em till the sun was burnin' hot. The ones who survived? They scattered so bad, not even two of 'em was left together.
11.12: After the fight, the people was like, 'Who was it that said, "Saul can't be our king?" Bring 'em here so we can kill 'em.'
11.13: But Saul said, 'Nah, not today. The Lord just gave Israel a huge victory—we ain't killin' nobody today.'
11.14: Then Samuel said, 'Aight, everybody, let's go to Gilgal and officially crown Saul as king.'
11.15: So everybody pulled up to Gilgal, made Saul king before the Lord, offered peace offerings, and had a big celebration. Israel turned up that day.

12.1: Then Samuel told all of Israel, 'Aight, I did what y'all wanted—I gave y'all a king.'
12.2: 'Now look—there he go, y'all king, walkin' ahead of y'all. Meanwhile, I'm old now, got gray hairs, and my sons are with y'all. I been leadin' y'all since I was a kid.'
12.3: 'So tell me—have I ever taken anything from y'all? Anybody's ox? Anybody's donkey? Did I cheat anybody? Did I take bribes to look the other way? If so, let me know—I'll pay it back.'
12.4: The people said, 'Nah, you never cheated us, oppressed us, or took nothin' from nobody.'
12.5: Samuel said, 'Aight, y'all heard that! The Lord and His anointed one are my witnesses today that I ain't do y'all dirty.' They replied, 'Yeah, we witness.'
12.6: Then Samuel told 'em, 'Look, it was the Lord who raised up Moses and Aaron and brought y'all ancestors outta Egypt.'
12.7: 'Now stand still while I run down how the Lord been good to y'all from the very beginning.'
12.8: 'When Jacob's people was stuck in Egypt, they cried out to the Lord, and He sent Moses and Aaron to get 'em out and bring 'em here.'
12.9: 'But soon as they got comfortable, they forgot the Lord. So He let their enemies take over—Sisera, the Philistines, and Moab's king all came through and started oppressin' them.'
12.10: 'Then they cried out again, sayin', "We messed up! We turned away from You and started worshipin' Baal and Ashtoreth. Please save us, and we'll serve You!"'
12.11: 'So the Lord sent y'all Jerubbaal (Gideon), Bedan, Jephthah, and even me to rescue y'all from your enemies. And y'all was safe again.'
12.12: 'But when y'all saw Nahash, king of the Ammonites, comin' for y'all, instead of trustin' God, y'all said, "Nah, we need a king to rule us!" even though God was already your King.'
12.13: 'Well, here he is—the king y'all asked for. The Lord gave him to y'all.'
12.14: 'Now listen—if y'all fear the Lord, serve Him, and obey Him, both you and your king will be straight with God.'
12.15: 'But if y'all don't obey and start wildin' again? The Lord's hand gon' be against y'all, just like He was against y'all ancestors.'
12.16: 'Now watch this—the Lord 'bout to show y'all a sign right now.'
12.17: 'Ain't it wheat harvest season right now? I'ma ask the Lord to send thunder and rain so y'all see just how serious y'all messed up by askin' for a king.'
12.18: Then Samuel prayed, and just like that, God sent thunder and rain. The people got shook and was terrified of the Lord and Samuel.
12.19: They told Samuel, 'Please pray for us! We already messed up so much, and now we added askin' for a king to our sins! Don't let us die!'
12.20: Samuel told 'em, 'Don't be scared. Yeah, y'all messed up, but don't turn away from the Lord. Y'all still gotta serve Him with all your heart.'
12.21: 'And don't start chasin' after nonsense—idols can't help or save y'all. They worthless.'
12.22: 'The Lord ain't gon' give up on y'all, 'cause His name too great. He chose y'all as His people, and that ain't changin'.'
12.23: 'And as for me? I'ma keep prayin' for y'all. I ain't gon' stop, 'cause that would be a sin against the Lord. Plus, I'ma keep teachin' y'all the right way.'
12.24: 'Y'all need to fear the Lord and serve Him for real, with all your heart. Just think about everything He's done for y'all.'
12.25: 'But if y'all keep actin' up and doin' wickedness? Y'all and your king gon' be wiped out.'

13.1: Saul had been king for a year, and by the time he hit his second year, he started picking his army.
13.2: He chose 3,000 soldiers—2,000 stayed with him in Michmash and Bethel, and the other 1,000 was with Jonathan in Gibeah. The rest? He sent 'em home.
13.3: Jonathan took the fight to the Philistine outpost at Geba and won. The Philistines heard 'bout it, and Saul put out a war announcement all over Israel: 'Yo, let every Hebrew hear this!'
13.4: All of Israel heard what happened, and the Philistines was mad. So Israel gathered with Saul at Gilgal, ready for whatever.
13.5: But the Philistines pulled up deep—they had 30,000 chariots, 6,000 horsemen, and troops as many as the sand on the beach. They set up camp at Michmash, east of Beth Aven.
13.6: When Israel saw how deep the Philistines rolled in, they got scared. Some ran and hid in caves, bushes, rocks, pits—wherever they could.
13.7: Others ran across the Jordan River to Gad and Gilead. Meanwhile, Saul was still at Gilgal, and his troops? Shakin' in their boots.
13.8: Saul waited seven days, just like Samuel told him. But when Samuel ain't show up, his troops started scatterin'.
13.9: So Saul said, 'Bring me the burnt offering and peace offering.' Then he did it himself.
13.10: And just as soon as he finished? Samuel showed up. Saul went out to greet him.
13.11: Samuel was like, 'What did you just do?!' Saul said, 'Look, man, I saw my troops leavin' me, you ain't show up on time, and the Philistines were closing in at Michmash—'
13.12: 'So I was like, "I gotta do somethin' before the Philistines attack!" So I forced myself to offer the burnt offering.'
13.13: Samuel shook his head, 'You played yourself. You ain't follow the Lord's orders. If you had, your kingdom would've lasted forever.'
13.14: 'But now? Your kingdom is done. The Lord already picked someone better than you, someone after His own heart, 'cause you ain't listen to Him.'
13.15: Then Samuel left Gilgal and went to Gibeah. Meanwhile, Saul checked his army—only 600 men left.
13.16: Saul, Jonathan, and the soldiers stayed in Gibeah, while the Philistines set up at Michmash.
13.17: Then the Philistine raiders split into three squads—one went toward Ophrah in Shual,
13.18: Another went toward Beth Horon, and the last toward the Valley of Zeboim, near the wilderness.
13.19: Israel had no blacksmiths—Philistines made sure of that. They ain't want the Hebrews makin' swords or spears.
13.20: So anytime an Israelite needed to sharpen a tool—plow, ax, sickle—they had to go to the Philistines.
13.21: And the Philistines charged them for it. Even to sharpen basic tools.
13.22: So when it was time for battle, guess what? Ain't nobody in Israel had a sword or spear—except Saul and Jonathan.
13.23: Meanwhile, the Philistine outpost took position at Michmash.

14.1: One day, Jonathan, Saul's son, told his armor-bearer, 'Ayo, let's go check out the Philistine outpost on the other side.' But he ain't tell his dad.
14.2: Meanwhile, Saul was chillin' on the outskirts of Gibeah, sittin' under a pomegranate tree at Migron with about 600 soldiers.
14.3: Ahijah, the priest from Shiloh, was there too, rockin' the ephod. But nobody knew Jonathan had already dipped.
14.4: To get to the Philistine outpost, Jonathan had to cross a narrow pass between two big ol' rocks—one called Bozez, the other Seneh.
14.5: One rock was facin' north toward Michmash, the other south toward Gibeah.
14.6: Jonathan told his armor-bearer, 'Look, let's go up to these uncircumcised Philistines. Maybe the Lord will help us out. 'Cause with God? It don't matter if we got a whole army or just a few—He can still win.'
14.7: His armor-bearer was like, 'I'm with you all the way. Do whatever you feel is right.'
14.8: Jonathan was like, 'Aight, here's the plan. We gon' step out and let them see us.'
14.9: 'If they tell us, "Stay put, we comin' to y'all," we won't move.'
14.10: 'But if they say, "Come up here," that's our sign that the Lord already gave us the win.'
14.11: So they stepped out, and the Philistines saw 'em. They laughed and said, 'Look at these Hebrews crawlin' out they hidey holes!'
14.12: Then the Philistines yelled, 'Come up here! We got somethin' for y'all!' Jonathan turned to his armor-bearer and said, 'That's our sign! Let's go!'
14.13: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and knees, with his armor-bearer right behind him. They started droppin' Philistines left and right.
14.14: That first attack? Jonathan and his guy took out 20 men in an area no bigger than half an acre.
14.15: Then the panic hit. In the Philistine camp, in the field—everybody started trippin'. Even the raiders freaked out. Then the ground started shaking. God was messin' with them for real.
14.16: Back in Gibeah, Saul's lookouts saw the Philistine army in full chaos—runnin' everywhere.
14.17: Saul was like, 'Wait… who's missing from our squad?' So they did a roll call and realized Jonathan and his armor-bearer was gone.
14.18: Saul told the priest, 'Bring the Ark of God!' (Back then, the Ark stayed with Israel.)
14.19: But while Saul was talkin' to the priest, the noise from the Philistine camp kept gettin' crazier. So Saul cut him off and said, 'Forget that! Let's go!'
14.20: Saul and his whole squad rushed into the battle, and guess what? The Philistines was fightin' EACH OTHER! Total confusion.
14.21: Even the Israelites who had been with the Philistines before, servin' them? They flipped sides and started fightin' for Saul and Jonathan.
14.22: Same with the Israelites that was hidin' in the mountains. When they saw the Philistines runnin'? They jumped in too!
14.23: That day, the Lord saved Israel, and the battle moved on to Beth Aven.
14.24: Now, the soldiers was struggling, 'cause Saul had made a dumb rule: 'Nobody eats until we finish beatin' our enemies—or else they cursed!'
14.25: They came up to a forest, and honey was drippin' everywhere.
14.26: But because of Saul's rule, nobody touched it, even though they was hungry as ever.
14.27: But Jonathan ain't know about the rule—so he dipped his staff in some honey, ate it, and felt better instantly.
14.28: Somebody told him, 'Bruh, your dad said anybody who eats today is cursed. Now look at us—we all about to pass out!'
14.29: Jonathan was like, 'Man, my dad messed up. Look at me—I ate some honey, and I feel good!'
14.30: 'If we woulda been eatin' today, we coulda whooped the Philistines even harder!'
14.31: By the time they chased the Philistines to Aijalon, the soldiers was dead tired.
14.32: So they rushed to the spoils, killin' sheep, oxen, and calves. But they ate the meat WITH the blood still in it.
14.33: Somebody told Saul, 'Yo, the people sinnin'—they eatin' with the blood!' Saul was like, 'Y'all messed up. Bring me a big stone right now!'
14.34: Then he told the people, 'Bring your animals here and kill 'em properly. Don't be sinnin' like this.' So everybody brought their animals and cooked them right.
14.35: Then Saul built an altar to the Lord—his first one.
14.36: Saul was like, 'Let's chase the Philistines all night and take all their stuff till morning!' The people said, 'Bet.' But the priest was like, 'Uh… shouldn't we ask God first?'
14.37: So Saul asked God, 'Should we chase 'em? You gon' give 'em to us?' But God ain't answer.
14.38: Saul was like, 'Something wrong. Somebody sinned today, and we gotta figure out who.'
14.39: 'I swear, even if it's Jonathan, my son—he gon' die.' But nobody said nothin'.
14.40: Saul said, 'Me and Jonathan on this side, everybody else on that side.' The people was like, 'Do what you gotta do.'
14.41: Then Saul asked God to show the truth, and the lot fell on him and Jonathan.
14.42: So he cast the lot again—this time it landed on Jonathan.
14.43: Saul was like, 'What did you do?!' Jonathan said, 'All I did was eat a lil' honey… so now I gotta die?'
14.44: Saul was serious. 'God help me if I don't kill you today, Jonathan.'
14.45: But the people was like, 'Nah, we ain't lettin' you kill him! Jonathan just helped us win this battle—he was workin' with God today!' So they saved Jonathan's life.
14.46: After that, Saul stopped chasing the Philistines, and they went back home.
14.47: Saul ruled over Israel and fought everybody—Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he went, he caused problems.
14.48: He built up his army, crushed the Amalekites, and saved Israel from its enemies.
14.49: Saul had three sons—Jonathan, Jishui, and Malchishua. His daughters were Merab and Michal.
14.50: His wife was Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz. His army commander? Abner, son of Saul's uncle Ner.
14.51: Saul's daddy was Kish, and Abner's daddy was Ner—both of them was sons of Abiel.
14.52: And every time Saul saw a strong warrior, he snatched him up for his army.

15.1: Samuel told Saul, 'The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over Israel. Now, you gotta listen to Him.'
15.2: 'This what the Lord says: Amalek messed up when they attacked My people back when they was leavin' Egypt.'
15.3: 'So now, I need you to wipe them out completely—every man, woman, child, ox, sheep, camel, and donkey. No survivors.'
15.4: So Saul gathered his troops at Telaim—200,000 foot soldiers plus 10,000 from Judah.
15.5: They rolled up on the Amalekite city and got ready to attack.
15.6: Saul told the Kenites, 'Ayo, y'all better dip before y'all get caught up in this. Y'all showed Israel love when we left Egypt, so I ain't tryna wipe y'all out too.' So the Kenites bounced.
15.7: Then Saul and his army crushed the Amalekites, from Havilah to Shur, near Egypt.
15.8: But instead of killin' everybody, Saul took King Agag alive and killed the rest of the Amalekites.
15.9: But Saul and his people kept all the best livestock—the sheep, oxen, and lambs. They only destroyed the weak stuff.
15.10: Then the Lord spoke to Samuel:
15.11: 'I regret makin' Saul king—he turned his back on Me and ain't do what I said.' Samuel was heartbroken and prayed all night.
15.12: Early next morning, Samuel went to find Saul. But folks told him, 'Yo, Saul set up a monument for himself in Carmel and then left for Gilgal.'
15.13: When Samuel found him, Saul was like, 'Blessed be the Lord! I did exactly what He said!'
15.14: Samuel was like, 'Then why do I hear sheep and oxen right now?'
15.15: Saul tried to cover up: 'Oh, the troops kept the best livestock to sacrifice to the Lord. But don't worry—we destroyed the rest!'
15.16: Samuel cut him off: 'Stop talking! Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.' Saul was like, 'Go ahead.'
15.17: Samuel said, 'Remember when you was small-time? The Lord still made you king.'
15.18: 'He sent you on a mission—wipe out the Amalekites, no mercy.'
15.19: 'So why you ain't obey? Why you kept the loot and did exactly what God said not to do?'
15.20: Saul tried to justify himself: 'I did obey! I took the troops, destroyed the Amalekites, and only brought back Agag.'
15.21: 'And okay, yeah, we kept the best livestock—but only to sacrifice to God!'
15.22: Samuel said, 'You think God wants sacrifices more than obedience? Nah. Obeying is better than sacrificing.'
15.23: 'Rebellion is just like witchcraft, and stubbornness is as bad as idolatry. Since you rejected the Lord's word? He just rejected you as king.'
15.24: Saul finally admitted, 'I messed up. I was scared of the people, so I did what they wanted instead of obeying God.'
15.25: 'Please forgive me! Come with me so I can worship the Lord!'
15.26: But Samuel said, 'Nah. You rejected the Lord, now He rejected you as king.'
15.27: Samuel turned to leave, but Saul grabbed his robe—and it tore!
15.28: Samuel turned back and said, 'Just like that, the Lord has torn the kingdom from you today. He already picked someone better than you.'
15.29: 'And don't think He gon' change His mind. God ain't human—He don't backtrack.'
15.30: Saul was desperate: 'I know I messed up! But at least honor me in front of the people! Come with me so I can worship the Lord!'
15.31: So Samuel went with him, and Saul worshiped.
15.32: Then Samuel said, 'Bring me King Agag.' Agag showed up all nervous, thinkin', 'Maybe they'll let me live.'
15.33: But Samuel said, 'Your sword made women childless? Now your mama gon' be childless too.' Then Samuel hacked Agag to pieces in Gilgal.
15.34: Then Samuel went back to Ramah, and Saul went to Gibeah.
15.35: Samuel never saw Saul again after that, but he still mourned for him. And the Lord regretted makin' Saul king.

16.1: The Lord told Samuel, 'How long you gon' sit here cryin' over Saul? I already rejected him as king. Get up, fill your horn with oil, and go to Jesse in Bethlehem—I already picked one of his sons to be king.'
16.2: Samuel was like, 'How I'ma do that? If Saul hears about it, he gon' kill me.' But the Lord said, 'Take a young cow with you and say you comin' to offer a sacrifice.'
16.3: 'Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I'ma tell you exactly who to anoint.'
16.4: Samuel did what God told him and went to Bethlehem. When the town elders saw him, they got shook and asked, 'Yo, you comin' in peace?'
16.5: Samuel said, 'Yeah, don't trip—I'm here to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get y'all selves ready and come with me.' Then he had Jesse and his sons get prepared for the sacrifice too.
16.6: When Samuel saw Eliab, he thought, 'Oh yeah, this gotta be the Lord's chosen one.'
16.7: But the Lord told Samuel, 'Nah, don't go off looks or height. I already rejected him. Humans look at the outside, but I look at the heart.'
16.8: Then Jesse brought up Abinadab, but Samuel said, 'Nope, not him either.'
16.9: Then Jesse brought up Shammah, but Samuel was like, 'Nah, not him either.'
16.10: Jesse ran through seven sons, but Samuel was like, 'The Lord ain't picked none of these.'
16.11: Samuel asked Jesse, 'You got any more sons?' Jesse said, 'Yeah, but he the youngest—he out watchin' the sheep.' Samuel said, 'Go get him. We ain't sittin' down 'til he gets here.'
16.12: So Jesse sent for him. David pulled up—he was young, handsome, and had bright eyes. The Lord said, 'That's the one. Get up and anoint him.'
16.13: So Samuel took his horn of oil and anointed David in front of his brothers. From that day on, the Spirit of the Lord was with David strong. Then Samuel left for Ramah.
16.14: Meanwhile, the Spirit of the Lord left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord started messin' with him.
16.15: Saul's servants told him, 'Yo, we can tell something is off with you—this spirit from God got you all messed up.'
16.16: 'Let us find somebody who can play the harp real good. Whenever that spirit comes on you, he'll play, and you'll feel better.'
16.17: Saul said, 'Find me somebody good at playin' and bring him to me.'
16.18: One of the servants said, 'I know a dude. Jesse's son, David—he play real good, plus he brave, smart, and good lookin'—and the Lord is with him.'
16.19: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, sayin', 'Send me David, your son—the one with the sheep.'
16.20: Jesse sent David to Saul with a donkey loaded with bread, wine, and a goat.
16.21: David came to Saul, stood before him, and Saul took a real liking to him—made him his armor-bearer.
16.22: Saul sent word back to Jesse, 'Let David stay with me—he cool with me.'
16.23: And whenever that evil spirit came on Saul, David would play his harp, and Saul would feel better—the spirit would leave him alone.

17.1: The Philistines gathered their army at Sochoh, a town in Judah, and camped between Sochoh and Azekah, in Ephes Dammim.
17.2: Saul and the Israelite army set up in the Valley of Elah, lining up against the Philistines.
17.3: The Philistines were on one mountain, the Israelites on another mountain, with a valley in between.
17.4: Then their champion stepped out—Goliath from Gath. This dude was huge—over nine feet tall.
17.5: He had a bronze helmet, a coat of armor that weighed 125 pounds.
17.6: Bronze armor on his legs, a huge javelin slung on his back.
17.7: His spear was massive, and the spearhead alone weighed 15 pounds. A shield-bearer walked ahead of him.
17.8: Goliath stepped forward and called out to Israel: 'Why y'all even tryna fight? Ain't I a Philistine? Ain't y'all just Saul's servants? Pick one man to fight me!'
17.9: 'If he kills me, we'll be y'all's slaves. But if I kill him, y'all gon' be our slaves.'
17.10: 'I challenge y'all today—send somebody out! Let's do this!'
17.11: Saul and all of Israel heard Goliath's words and was shook—straight-up terrified.
17.12: David was the youngest son of Jesse, an old man from Bethlehem, Judah.
17.13: Jesse's three oldest sons had already gone to war with Saul—Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah.
17.14: David was the youngest—his three brothers followed Saul,
17.15: But David still went back and forth between Saul and home to take care of his father's sheep in Bethlehem.
17.16: For 40 days, Goliath came out every morning and evening to challenge Israel.
17.17: One day, Jesse told David, 'Take this grain and bread to your brothers at the camp.'
17.18: 'Also, take these ten cheeses to the commander. Check on your brothers and bring back word.'
17.19: Saul and the army was in the Valley of Elah, facing off against the Philistines.
17.20: David got up early, left the sheep with a caretaker, packed up the food, and headed to the camp.
17.21: By the time he got there, the armies were lined up, getting ready to fight.
17.22: David dropped off the supplies with the keeper and ran up to greet his brothers.
17.23: While he was talking, Goliath showed up again, saying the same challenge as before—and David heard him.
17.24: As soon as the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they ran in fear.
17.25: They told David, 'You seen this dude?! He's disrespecting Israel! The king said whoever kills him gets money, his daughter, and tax-free living!'
17.26: David was like, 'Wait, what's the reward? And who this uncircumcised Philistine think he is disrespecting God's army?!'
17.27: The soldiers repeated the same reward.
17.28: David's oldest brother, Eliab, heard him talking and got mad: 'Why you even here? Who watchin' them few sheep? I know you just tryna be nosy.'
17.29: David said, 'What did I do now? I'm just askin' a question!'
17.30: Then he turned to somebody else and asked again, and got the same answer.
17.31: When Saul heard David was talkin' like this, he sent for him.
17.32: David told Saul, 'Ain't nobody gotta be scared—I'll fight him!'
17.33: Saul was like, 'Boy, you can't fight him—you just a kid! He been a warrior since birth.'
17.34: David said, 'I take care of my daddy's sheep. When a lion or bear came, I handled it.'
17.35: 'I chased it down, snatched the lamb back, and if it came at me, I grabbed it by the beard and killed it.'
17.36: 'I done killed lions and bears—this Philistine ain't no different. He been disrespectin' God's army, and he gon' get handled.'
17.37: 'The Lord saved me from the lion and the bear—He gon' save me from this Philistine too.' Saul said, 'Go ahead then. May the Lord be with you.'
17.38: Saul tried to put his armor on David—gave him a helmet, a coat of armor.
17.39: David strapped on Saul's sword, tried to walk, then said, 'Nah, I can't do this—I ain't used to it.' So he took it off.
17.40: Instead, he grabbed his staff, picked up five smooth stones, put 'em in his shepherd's bag, and had his sling ready.
17.41: Goliath walked toward David, with his shield-bearer in front of him.
17.42: When Goliath saw David, he laughed. 'This the best y'all got?! A lil' pretty boy?!'
17.43: He said, 'What am I, a dog?! You comin' at me with a stick?!' Then he cursed David by his gods.
17.44: Goliath said, 'Come here! I'ma feed your body to the birds and wild animals!'
17.45: David said, 'You come at me with swords and spears, but I come at you in the name of the Lord!'
17.46: 'Today, the Lord gon' hand you over to me—I'ma knock you down, cut your head off, and feed your army's bodies to the birds and beasts!'
17.47: 'Then everybody gon' know God don't need weapons to save—this battle belongs to the Lord!'
17.48: Goliath stepped forward—David ran toward him!
17.49: David reached in his bag, pulled out a stone, and slung it—BOOM! The stone sank into Goliath's forehead and he fell face-first into the ground.
17.50: David killed Goliath with a sling and a stone—no sword needed.
17.51: Then David ran up, took Goliath's own sword, finished him off, and cut his head clean off. When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they ran!
17.52: Israel and Judah chased them down all the way to Ekron, killin' them as they ran.
17.53: After the chase, Israel plundered the Philistine camp.
17.54: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but kept his armor in his tent.
17.55: When Saul saw David step up against Goliath, he asked his army commander, Abner, 'Who's this kid's daddy?' Abner said, 'I don't know.'
17.56: Saul said, 'Find out who his father is.'
17.57: When David came back with Goliath's head, Abner took him to Saul.
17.58: Saul asked, 'Who's your father, young man?' David said, 'Jesse, from Bethlehem.'

18.1: After David finished talkin' to Saul, Jonathan's spirit was tied to David's—he loved him like a brother.
18.2: Saul kept David with him, wouldn't even let him go back home.
18.3: Jonathan and David made a covenant, 'cause Jonathan loved David like his own soul.
18.4: Jonathan took off his royal robe and gave it to David—along with his armor, sword, bow, and belt.
18.5: David did whatever Saul asked, and he did it well. So Saul put him in charge of the army. Everybody respected him, including Saul's servants.
18.6: One day, when David came back from fightin' the Philistines, all the women came out the cities singing and dancing for Saul, playin' tambourines and music.
18.7: But listen to what they was singin': 'Saul killed his thousands, But David killed his ten-thousands!'
18.8: Saul was heated. He was like, 'Hold up—y'all givin' David ten-thousands, but only givin' me thousands?! What's next? He takin' the throne too?!'
18.9: From that day on, Saul kept his eye on David—he wasn't feelin' him no more.
18.10: The next day, that evil spirit from the Lord came back on Saul, and he started actin' crazy in the house.
18.11: Saul grabbed his spear and threw it at David, tryna pin him to the wall. But David dodged him—twice.
18.12: Saul started getting scared of David 'cause he could see the Lord was with David—but not with him no more.
18.13: So Saul sent David away and made him a commander over 1,000 soldiers.
18.14: David was smart and successful in everything he did, 'cause the Lord was with him.
18.15: When Saul saw how well David was doin', he got even more scared.
18.16: But all of Israel and Judah loved David, 'cause he was always out in the field with them.
18.17: Then Saul told David, 'Aight, I'ma give you my oldest daughter, Merab. Just keep fightin' the Lord's battles.' But in his heart, Saul was hopin' David would die in battle.
18.18: David was humble about it: 'Who am I? Why should I be the king's son-in-law? My family ain't nobody special.'
18.19: But when it was time to marry Merab, Saul gave her to some other dude, Adriel.
18.20: But Saul's other daughter, Michal, had a thing for David. And when Saul heard about it? He was happy.
18.21: Saul thought, 'Aha! She gon' be a trap for him—the Philistines will take him out!' So Saul told David, 'Aight, now you really gon' be my son-in-law.'
18.22: Saul even told his servants, 'Go tell David on the low that the king really likes you, and so do his servants. You should become his son-in-law.'
18.23: But when they told David, he said, 'Y'all think I can just marry the king's daughter like that? I'm broke!'
18.24: Saul's servants took his words back to him.
18.25: So Saul told them, 'Tell David he don't need no dowry—just bring me 100 Philistine foreskins as revenge on my enemies.' (Saul was hopin' David would die tryin' to get them.)
18.26: When David heard the offer, he was like, 'Bet.' He was cool with it.
18.27: So David and his men went out and killed 200 Philistines—brought back double the foreskins to Saul. Then Saul gave him Michal as his wife.
18.28: Now Saul saw for sure that the Lord was with David—and that Michal really loved him.
18.29: Saul got even more scared of David—from that day on, he saw him as his enemy.
18.30: Whenever the Philistine rulers went to war, David was always more successful than Saul's other officers. His name just kept growin'.

19.1: Saul straight up told Jonathan and his servants that he wanted David dead. But Jonathan wasn't havin' it—he loved David like a brother.
19.2: Jonathan warned David, 'My father tryna kill you. Go hide somewhere 'til morning, and I'ma talk to him. I'll let you know what's up.'
19.3: 'I'ma go out there, talk to my dad in the field near you, and see where his head at. Whatever he say, I'ma tell you.'
19.4: Jonathan spoke up for David to his father Saul: 'Look, don't be wildin'—David ain't did nothin' to you. Matter fact, he been nothin' but good to you.'
19.5: 'He put his life on the line to take down Goliath, and God used him to save Israel. You saw it yourself—you was happy! So why you tryna kill an innocent man for no reason?'
19.6: Saul actually listened to Jonathan and swore, 'As the Lord lives, I won't kill him.'
19.7: Jonathan went back to David, told him what happened, and brought him back to Saul. For a while, everything was cool again.
19.8: Another war popped off, and David went out and handled the Philistines again, takin' 'em down bad.
19.9: But then, that evil spirit from the Lord came back on Saul while he was sittin' in the house, spear in hand. David was playin' the harp like usual.
19.10: Then Saul threw his spear at David again, tryna pin him to the wall! But David dodged and got outta there that night.
19.11: Saul sent men to watch David's house and kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him: 'If you don't leave tonight, you dead by tomorrow morning.'
19.12: So Michal helped David escape through a window—he ran for his life.
19.13: Then she took an idol, laid it in the bed, covered it with blankets, and put some goat hair on the pillow to make it look like David.
19.14: When Saul's men came to grab David, she told them, 'He sick.'
19.15: Saul was like, 'I don't care—bring him to me in the bed, I'ma kill him myself.'
19.16: When the men went in, they found the fake David in the bed.
19.17: Saul snapped on Michal, 'Why you lie for him?! You helped my enemy escape!' Michal said, 'He told me he'd kill me if I ain't help him!'
19.18: David ran straight to Samuel in Ramah and told him everything Saul was tryna do. They stayed in Naioth.
19.19: Saul found out David was at Naioth and sent men to grab him.
19.20: But when Saul's men got there, they saw Samuel and the prophets prophesying. Then the Spirit of God hit Saul's men, and they started prophesyin' too!
19.21: Saul heard about it and sent another group—same thing happened. Then he sent a third group—same thing!
19.22: Finally, Saul went himself to find David. When he got to the big well in Sechu, he asked, 'Where Samuel and David at?' Somebody said, 'They at Naioth in Ramah.'
19.23: Saul headed to Naioth, but before he even got there, the Spirit of God hit him too! He started prophesyin' the whole way there!
19.24: By the time he got to Samuel, Saul was stripped down, prophesyin' in the middle of everybody. He was laid out naked all day and night. That's why folks started sayin', 'Dang, is Saul a prophet too now?!'

20.1: David ran from Naioth in Ramah and went straight to Jonathan like, 'Yo, what did I do?! Why your dad tryna kill me?'
20.2: Jonathan was like, 'Nah, that ain't happenin'! My dad don't do nothing without tellin' me first. He wouldn't keep this from me.'
20.3: David swore on it: 'Bruh, your pops knows we tight—he ain't gon' tell you 'cause he don't want you stressin'. But I promise you, I'm one step from death.'
20.4: Jonathan said, 'Whatever you need, I got you.'
20.5: David told him, 'Tomorrow the king expectin' me at dinner. Let me hide in the field 'til the third night.'
20.6: 'If your dad asks where I'm at, tell him I went home to Bethlehem for a family sacrifice.'
20.7: 'If he cool with that, I'm safe. But if he flips out, that means he tryna kill me.'
20.8: 'Look, we in a covenant before the Lord. If I'm guilty of somethin', just kill me yourself—but don't hand me over to your father.'
20.9: Jonathan was like, 'Man, don't say that! If I knew my father was tryna kill you, you think I wouldn't tell you?!'
20.10: David asked, 'How I'ma know what he say? Who gon' tell me?'
20.11: Jonathan was like, 'Come on, let's go outside.' So they stepped into the field.
20.12: Jonathan said, 'God be my witness. After I talk to my dad tomorrow or the next day, if he still cool with you, I'ma tell you.'
20.13: 'But if he tryna kill you, I swear I'ma warn you so you can escape. May the Lord be with you like He was with my father.'
20.14: 'And when you become king, don't forget about me.'
20.15: 'Even when God wipes out all your enemies, don't cut off my family.'
20.16: Jonathan made a covenant with David, saying, 'May God punish David's enemies.'
20.17: Jonathan had David swear again—'cause he loved him like his own soul.
20.18: Then Jonathan told David, 'Tomorrow's the New Moon feast—your absence gon' be noticed.'
20.19: 'In three days, go back to the hiding spot near the Stone of Ezel.'
20.20: 'I'ma shoot three arrows like I'm target practicin'.'
20.21: 'If I tell the boy, "The arrows are close by," you good—come back.'
20.22: 'But if I say, "The arrows are farther!" that means you gotta run, 'cause God sendin' you away.'
20.23: 'And remember—this pact is forever between us before the Lord.'
20.24: David hid in the field, and when the New Moon feast started, Saul was in his usual seat.
20.25: Jonathan stood next to him, Abner was beside Saul—but David's seat was empty.
20.26: Saul ain't say nothin' the first day, thinkin', 'Maybe David unclean.'
20.27: The next day, when David was still missing, Saul asked Jonathan, 'Why ain't Jesse's son come eat?'
20.28: Jonathan said, 'David asked to go home to Bethlehem.'
20.29: 'He told me his family was havin' a sacrifice, and his brother wanted him there. So I let him go.'
20.30: Saul LOST IT on Jonathan: 'You son of a rebellious woman! You really ridin' for Jesse's son?! You shamin' yourself and your mama!'
20.31: 'As long as David alive, you ain't never gon' be king! Now go get him so I can kill him!'
20.32: Jonathan snapped back: 'Why he gotta die?! What did he even do?!'
20.33: Saul threw his spear at his own son! That's when Jonathan knew—his dad was dead serious about killin' David.
20.34: Jonathan stormed away from the table, mad as hell, and didn't eat that day—he was hurt over how his dad treated David.
20.35: The next morning, Jonathan went to the field with a young servant, as planned.
20.36: He shot the arrow, then told the boy, 'Run and find it!'
20.37: As the boy ran, Jonathan yelled, 'Ain't the arrow farther than you?!'
20.38: Then he shouted, 'Hurry up! Don't wait!' (That was David's cue to run.)
20.39: The boy had no clue what was happenin'—only Jonathan and David knew.
20.40: Jonathan gave his bow and arrows to the boy and told him, 'Take these back to the city.'
20.41: As soon as the boy left, David came out of hiding. He bowed before Jonathan three times, crying.
20.42: Jonathan told David, 'Go in peace. We both swore before the Lord—this bond lasts forever, between us and our kids.'
20.43: Then David left, and Jonathan went back to the city.

21.1: David rolled up to Nob and met with Ahimelech, the priest. Ahimelech was lookin' nervous and asked, 'Why you out here by yourself? Where yo' people at?'
21.2: David lied and said, 'The king sent me on a secret mission. Ain't nobody supposed to know about it. My crew meetin' me somewhere else.'
21.3: 'But listen—you got any food? Just give me five loaves of bread, or whatever you got.'
21.4: Ahimelech was like, 'Ain't no regular bread here, only the holy bread—but I'll give it to you if y'all been stayin' away from women.'
21.5: David said, 'We been clean—ain't been with no women in three days. Besides, this bread just regular now, even though it started as holy.'
21.6: So Ahimelech gave him the holy bread, 'cause that was the only bread they had left—the showbread from the Lord's table.
21.7: But check this—one of Saul's men was there too. His name was Doeg the Edomite, head of Saul's shepherds. And he was watchin'.
21.8: David asked Ahimelech, 'You got a spear or sword? I ain't got no weapon 'cause the king's business was urgent.'
21.9: Ahimelech was like, 'Only thing here is Goliath's sword—the same one you took when you killed him. It's behind the ephod, wrapped in a cloth. You can take it if you want.'
21.10: David said, 'Ain't no sword like that one. Gimme that.' Then he grabbed it and got outta there fast.
21.11: David ran to Gath and showed up at King Achish's palace. But Achish's servants was whisperin', 'Ain't this David, the king of Israel? Ain't he the one they sing about?'
21.12: David heard what they was sayin' and got shook—he knew this wasn't a safe place.
21.13: So he started actin' crazy—scratchin' on doors, droolin' all over his beard like he lost his mind.
21.14: Achish looked at his servants and said, 'Y'all really brought me a madman?!'
21.15: 'I got enough crazy people around me—why y'all bring him here? Get him outta my house!'

22.1: David left there and hid out in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's people heard about it, they went to meet him.
22.2: Folks who was down bad—broke, in debt, or just fed up with life—started gatherin' around David. He became their leader, and soon he had about 400 men ridin' with him.
22.3: Then David went to Mizpah in Moab and told the king of Moab, 'Please let my parents stay with you 'til I figure out what God wants me to do.'
22.4: So David left his parents there in Moab, and they stayed as long as he was in hiding.
22.5: Then the prophet Gad came and told David, 'Don't stay here—go back to Judah.' So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
22.6: Meanwhile, Saul heard where David and his men were hidin'. He was chillin' in Gibeah, sittin' under a tamarisk tree, spear in hand, surrounded by his servants.
22.7: Saul told them, 'Listen up, Benjamites! Y'all really think this son of Jesse gon' hook y'all up with land and promotions?'
22.8: 'All of y'all conspirin' against me! Ain't nobody told me Jonathan made a deal with David. Ain't nobody ridin' for me! Y'all lettin' David set up on me like this!'
22.9: Then Doeg the Edomite (the same dude that saw David at Nob) spoke up: 'I saw David in Nob with Ahimelech, the priest.'
22.10: 'Ahimelech prayed to God for him, gave him food, and even gave him Goliath's sword!'
22.11: Saul called for Ahimelech and his whole priestly family from Nob. They all pulled up before the king.
22.12: Saul looked at Ahimelech and said, 'Yo, son of Ahitub, you hear me?!' Ahimelech answered, 'Yes, my king?'
22.13: Saul snapped, 'Why you helpin' David?! You gave him food, a weapon, and even prayed to God for him! Now he plottin' on me!'
22.14: Ahimelech tried to explain, 'But wait, ain't David your most loyal soldier? Your son-in-law? A man you trust to lead your armies?'
22.15: 'And this ain't even the first time I prayed for him! I ain't know nothin' about no plot against you!'
22.16: Saul wasn't tryin' to hear it. 'Nah, you gon' die, you and your whole family!'
22.17: Then Saul told his guards, 'Kill the Lord's priests! They ridin' with David and didn't tell me!' But his men refused to touch the priests.
22.18: So Saul turned to Doeg: 'You do it!' Doeg slaughtered 85 priests that day—all of them wearing priestly robes.
22.19: Then Doeg went to Nob and killed everybody—men, women, kids, even babies. He wiped out oxen, donkeys, and sheep too.
22.20: But one priest survived—Abiathar, son of Ahimelech. He ran and found David.
22.21: Abiathar told David what happened—how Saul had killed all the priests.
22.22: David sighed, 'Man… I knew it! When I saw Doeg that day, I knew he was gon' tell Saul. This my fault.'
22.23: 'Stay with me. Don't be scared. Saul want me dead too, so you safer with me than anywhere else.'

23.1: Some folks came and told David, 'Yo, the Philistines out here wildin' on Keilah, robbing their grain and messing up the city!'
23.2: David went straight to God and asked, 'Should I go handle these Philistines?' And the Lord told him, 'Go ahead and take 'em down. Save Keilah.'
23.3: But David's men weren't feeling it. They said, 'Bruh, we already shook just being in Judah. Now you tryna take us to fight Philistine armies in Keilah?'
23.4: So David went back to God for confirmation. And the Lord told him again, 'Go down to Keilah. I got you. You will win.'
23.5: So David and his crew rolled up, fought the Philistines, put them down with a major blow, and took all their livestock. David saved Keilah, just like God said.
23.6: When Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech, escaped and linked up with David in Keilah, he brought the ephod with him.
23.7: Word got to Saul that David was in Keilah, and Saul got hype. He said, 'God done put him right in my hands! He locked himself in a city with gates and bars. Easy win.'
23.8: So Saul gathered his army and got ready to roll down to Keilah to trap David and his men.
23.9: But David got wind of Saul's plan. He told Abiathar the priest, 'Bring the ephod over here. We need to ask God something real quick.'
23.10: Then David prayed, 'Lord, I heard Saul is coming to tear this city up just to get to me.'
23.11: 'Will the people of Keilah turn me in? Is Saul really coming like they say?' And the Lord answered, 'Yeah, he coming.'
23.12: Then David asked, 'But will the people of Keilah give me up to Saul?' And the Lord said, 'Yeah, they will.'
23.13: So David and his 600 men got up outta there quick and went wherever they could. When Saul heard David had escaped, he called off the attack.
23.14: David and his crew stayed hidden in the wilderness, moving through the mountains of Ziph. Saul was on the hunt every day, but God made sure Saul never caught him.
23.15: David knew Saul was out there trying to kill him, so he kept low in the forests of Ziph.
23.16: Then Jonathan, Saul's son, pulled up to David and gave him some real talk, reminding him that God got him.
23.17: Jonathan told David, 'Don't trip. My father ain't gonna find you. You gonna be king of Israel, and I'll be right there beside you. Even my dad knows that!'
23.18: So the two of them made another covenant before the Lord. Then Jonathan went back home, and David stayed in the woods.
23.19: Then some dudes from Ziph ran to Saul in Gibeah and said, 'Yo, David hiding in our woods, up in the strongholds on the hill of Hachilah, south of Jeshimon.'
23.20: 'Come down here, king, just like you been wanting. We'll make sure you get him.'
23.21: Saul was feeling himself and said, 'Bless y'all for looking out for me! Y'all really got my back.'
23.22: 'Now go double-check where he at. Find out his hiding spots. I hear he real slick and hard to catch.'
23.23: 'Look everywhere he might be hiding. Then come back and tell me, and I'll roll out with y'all. If he's anywhere in Judah, I'll find him!'
23.24: So the Ziphites left to go track David, while Saul was still making plans. Meanwhile, David and his men were hiding deep in the Wilderness of Maon.
23.25: Saul and his men went searching for David, and when David got word, he dipped down to a big rock in the Wilderness of Maon.
23.26: Saul's army was on one side of the mountain, and David's men were on the other. Saul was closing in, about to trap David completely.
23.27: But just then, a messenger ran up to Saul saying, 'Yo! Hurry back! The Philistines are attacking the land!'
23.28: So Saul had to break off the chase and go fight the Philistines instead. That's why they named that place the Rock of Escape.
23.29: After that, David left and stayed in the strongholds at En-Gedi.

24.1: After Saul finished dealin' with the Philistines, somebody came up to him like, 'Yo, David hidin' in the Wilderness of En Gedi.'
24.2: Saul grabbed 3,000 of his best soldiers and went out to find David and his men near the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
24.3: On the way, Saul stopped by some sheep pens where there was a cave. He went inside to handle his business—but David and his men was already deep inside that cave!
24.4: David's men whispered, 'Ayo, this it! God done put Saul in your hands! Do whatever you wanna do to him!' David snuck up and cut off a piece of Saul's robe—real quiet.
24.5: But soon as he did it, David started feelin' guilty.
24.6: He told his men, 'I can't do Saul like that. He's still the Lord's anointed—I can't raise my hand against him.'
24.7: So David shut his men down—wouldn't let them touch Saul. Saul finished up, left the cave, and went on his way.
24.8: Then David stepped out the cave and called after Saul: 'My king!' When Saul turned around, David bowed low.
24.9: David asked, 'Why you listenin' to folks sayin' I'm out to get you?'
24.10: 'You just saw with your own eyes—God put you in my hands today. Some of my guys told me to kill you, but I didn't!'
24.11: 'Look, I even cut off a piece of your robe! If I wanted you dead, you'd be dead!'
24.12: 'Let God judge between us. I ain't out for revenge, but I'll let God handle it.'
24.13: 'Like the old saying goes, "Evil people do evil things." But I ain't one of 'em.'
24.14: 'Why you chasin' me, king? I'm nobody. I'm just a flea, a stray dog.'
24.15: 'Let God handle this. Let Him judge me right.'
24.16: When David finished talkin', Saul was shook. He started cryin'.
24.17: Saul told David, 'You a better man than me. You treated me good, but I been tryna do you dirty.'
24.18: 'Today, you coulda killed me, but you let me live. Who does that to an enemy?'
24.19: 'May the Lord bless you for sparin' me today.'
24.20: 'I know now—you gon' be king for sure. God already settin' you up for the throne.'
24.21: 'Just promise me one thing—don't wipe out my family after I'm gone. Keep my name alive.'
24.22: David swore to Saul, then Saul went back home, but David and his men stayed in the stronghold.

25.1: Samuel died, and all of Israel mourned for him. They buried him in Ramah, his hometown. David moved on to the Wilderness of Paran.
25.2: There was a rich man in Maon named Nabal. He had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats, and he was out in Carmel shearin' his sheep.
25.3: His wife, Abigail, was smart and beautiful—but Nabal was rude and reckless. He was from Caleb's family.
25.4: David heard Nabal was shearin' his sheep while he was out in the wilderness.
25.5: So David sent ten of his men to greet Nabal in his name.
25.6: They told Nabal, 'Peace to you, your house, and everything you got!'
