25.7: 'We know you got your sheep shearers workin'—just so you know, we never messed with them. We never stole from them while they was out in Carmel.'
25.8: 'Ask your men—they'll tell you. Since today's a feast day, could you spare somethin' for us?'
25.9: David's men told Nabal the message, then waited for his response.
25.10: Nabal snapped, 'Who David think he is? Who this son of Jesse? These days, servants runnin' away from their masters left and right.'
25.11: 'You think I'm just gon' give my food, water, and meat to some random men I don't even know?'
25.12: David's men turned around and went back, tellin' him everything Nabal said.
25.13: David was HOT. He told his men, 'Strap up!' 400 men geared up, while 200 stayed behind to guard their supplies.
25.14: One of Nabal's servants ran to Abigail and told her what went down.
25.15: 'Look, David's men been nothin' but good to us. They never harmed us or stole from us. They actually protected us while we was in the fields.'
25.16: 'They was like a wall around us, day and night, while we took care of the sheep.'
25.17: 'Ma'am, you gotta do somethin'—David is comin' for us. Nabal don't listen to nobody. He reckless.'
25.18: Abigail didn't waste no time. She packed up 200 loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five dressed sheep, roasted grain, 100 raisin clusters, and 200 fig cakes—loaded it all on donkeys.
25.19: She sent her servants ahead of her, tellin' 'em, 'Go on, I'll catch up.' She didn't tell Nabal.
25.20: As Abigail rode up on a donkey, she saw David and his men comin' her way.
25.21: David had just been ventin', 'I protected everything this fool owned, and this how he repays me?!'
25.22: 'May God do worse to me if by morning, every man in Nabal's house ain't dead.'
25.23: When Abigail saw David, she jumped off her donkey, fell on her face, and bowed before him.
25.24: She said, 'My lord, blame me! Please listen to me.'
25.25: 'Please don't take Nabal serious—his name means "fool," and he act just like it! I ain't see your men when they came.'
25.26: 'The Lord stopped you from doin' somethin' you'd regret. Let all your enemies be like Nabal.'
25.27: 'Take this gift I brought for your men.'
25.28: 'Please forgive my husband's foolishness. God got big plans for you, David! You fight His battles, and you stay righteous.'
25.29: 'Somebody tryna kill you, but your life is in God's hands. Your enemies? He gon' sling 'em away like a rock from a sling.'
25.30: 'When God makes you king over Israel, this moment won't haunt you.'
25.31: 'You ain't gotta regret killin' innocent people outta anger. When that time comes, remember me.'
25.32: David took a deep breath, 'Blessed be the Lord for sendin' you to me today!'
25.33: 'Bless you for keepin' me from killin' outta anger!'
25.34: 'If you ain't come, by morning Nabal's house would've been wiped out.'
25.35: David accepted her gift and said, 'Go in peace—I heard you out.'
25.36: Abigail went home, and Nabal was in there drunk off his mind, throwin' a feast like he was a king.
25.37: She ain't tell him nothin' 'til the next morning. When he sobered up, she told him everything.
25.38: Soon as he heard it, his heart gave out. He turned stiff like stone. Ten days later, the Lord struck him, and he died.
25.39: David heard Nabal was dead and said, 'Praise the Lord for avengin' me! He stopped me from doin' evil and paid Nabal back Himself.'
25.40: Then David sent messengers to Abigail, askin' her to be his wife.
25.41: She bowed low and said, 'I'd be honored to be David's servant—even just to wash his men's feet.'
25.42: She got on her donkey with her five maids, went with David's messengers, and became his wife.
25.43: David also married Ahinoam from Jezreel, so he had two wives now.
25.44: Meanwhile, Saul took Michal, David's first wife, and gave her to another man named Palti.

26.1: The Ziphites ran up to Saul again, tellin' him, 'David hidin' in the Hill of Hachilah, across from Jeshimon.'
26.2: Saul grabbed 3,000 of his best soldiers and rolled out to the Wilderness of Ziph to find David.
26.3: Saul set up camp at Hachilah by the road, but David stayed out in the wilderness. When David heard Saul was comin', he sent spies to confirm it.
26.4: David sent out his spies and got confirmation—yep, Saul really out here lookin' for him again.
26.5: David went to check out Saul's camp and saw where Saul and his general, Abner, were sleepin'. Saul was in the middle, surrounded by his men.
26.6: David turned to his crew and said, 'Who ridin' with me into Saul's camp?' Abishai (Joab's brother) stepped up, 'I got you.'
26.7: That night, David and Abishai snuck into the camp. Saul was knocked out, his spear stuck in the ground by his head, and his army was sleepin' all around him.
26.8: Abishai whispered, 'Ayo, God really put your enemy in your hands! Let me run this spear through him—one hit, I promise.'
26.9: David shook his head, 'Nah, we ain't touchin' God's anointed.'
26.10: 'God gon' handle him—either he gon' die naturally, or he gon' die in battle.'
26.11: 'We ain't doin' it. Just grab his spear and his water jug, and let's go.'
26.12: David snatched the spear and jug, and they dipped. Nobody saw them, 'cause God put everybody into a deep sleep.
26.13: David got to the top of a hill, far enough away, and shouted down at Saul's camp.
26.14: David yelled at Abner, 'Ayo, Abner! You ain't gon' answer me?!' Abner woke up and shouted back, 'Who dat callin' out to the king?!'
26.15: David clowned him, 'Bruh, ain't you supposed to be Saul's top guy? How you let somebody walk right up on the king like that?!'
26.16: 'You failed, man. Somebody coulda killed your king tonight. You deserve to die for that. Look, where Saul's spear and water jug at?'
26.17: Saul recognized David's voice and said, 'Is that you, my son David?'
26.18: David said, 'Yeah, it's me. But why you still out here chasin' me? What did I do?!'
26.19: 'If God sent you after me, then fine. But if people hyped you up, then may God curse them, 'cause they makin' me run from my home, like I don't even belong to God's people.'
26.20: 'Why you treatin' me like I'm a nobody? Like I'm some flea you tryna squash? Like a partridge you tryna hunt in the mountains?'
26.21: Saul broke down, 'I messed up. Come back, David. I ain't gon' try to hurt you no more. You spared my life today. I was a fool.'
26.22: David held up Saul's spear, 'Here it is. Send one of your guys to come get it.'
26.23: 'God gon' reward people who do right. He put you in my hands, but I refused to touch His anointed.'
26.24: 'Just like I spared your life today, I hope God looks out for me too.'
26.25: Saul blessed David, 'You gon' do great things and win big.' Then Saul went home, and David went his own way.

27.1: David was thinkin' to himself, 'Man, one day Saul gon' catch me. Best move is to dip to Philistine territory. Then Saul gon' give up tryna find me.'
27.2: So David took his 600 men and went to Gath, to stay with King Achish, son of Maoch.
27.3: David and his crew lived in Gath with Achish—each man with his family. David had his two wives: Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow.
27.4: When Saul heard David was in Gath, he stopped lookin' for him.
27.5: David told Achish, 'If I got favor with you, let me live in one of the country towns. Ain't no reason for me to be in the royal city with you.'
27.6: So Achish gave David the town of Ziklag—and from then on, Ziklag belonged to the kings of Judah.
27.7: David stayed in Philistine land for a year and four months.
27.8: David and his men went out raiding the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites—the folks who lived in that land before Israel came.
27.9: Every time David attacked, he left nobody alive—men or women. He took their sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothes, then went back to Achish.
27.10: Achish would ask, 'Where y'all raid today?' David would lie and say, 'We hit parts of Judah, Jerahmeel, or the Kenites.'
27.11: David made sure not to leave any survivors, so nobody could run back and tell Achish the truth.
27.12: Achish trusted David, thinkin', 'Man, he really turned on Israel. He stuck with me now.'

28.1: The Philistines got their armies ready for war against Israel, and King Achish told David, 'You already know you and your men gotta roll with me into battle.'
28.2: David told Achish, 'You already know what I'm capable of.' Achish said, 'Bet. I'm makin' you my top bodyguard for life.'
28.3: By now, Samuel was dead, and all of Israel mourned and buried him in Ramah. Meanwhile, Saul had kicked out all the mediums and spiritists.
28.4: The Philistines set up camp at Shunem, so Saul gathered his army at Gilboa.
28.5: When Saul saw how deep the Philistines' army was, he got shook—his heart was poundin'.
28.6: He tried askin' God what to do, but the Lord wasn't answerin'—no dreams, no Urim, no prophets.
28.7: So Saul told his servants, 'Find me a woman that can talk to spirits, so I can ask her what to do.' His men told him, 'There's a medium in En Dor.'
28.8: Saul disguised himself, put on regular clothes, and took two men with him. They rolled up to the woman at night, and Saul said, 'I need you to bring up a spirit for me.'
28.9: But the woman was like, 'You know Saul banned all the mediums. You tryna set me up to get killed?!'
28.10: Saul swore to her, 'I promise on the Lord's name, you won't be punished for this.'
28.11: She asked, 'Who you want me to bring up?' Saul said, 'Samuel.'
28.12: Soon as she saw Samuel, she screamed and said, 'Wait a minute—you Saul! You tricked me!'
28.13: Saul told her, 'Don't be scared. What you see?' She said, 'I see a spirit comin' up from the ground.'
28.14: Saul asked, 'What he look like?' She said, 'An old man wearin' a robe.' Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down.
28.15: Samuel was not happy: 'Why you botherin' me?! Why you draggin' me back up?!' Saul answered, 'Man, I'm stressed out! The Philistines at war with me, God left me, and I ain't gettin' no answers. I need you to tell me what to do!'
28.16: Samuel was like, 'If God left you and turned against you, why you askin' me?'
28.17: 'Didn't I tell you before? The Lord already took the kingdom from you and gave it to David.'
28.18: 'This happenin' 'cause you ain't listen when God told you to wipe out Amalek.'
28.19: 'And now, the Lord gon' hand over Israel to the Philistines. By this time tomorrow, you and your sons gon' be dead.'
28.20: Saul collapsed, straight-up laid out on the floor—terrified and weak from not eatin' all day.
28.21: The woman walked over to Saul, saw how shook he was, and said, 'Look, I did what you asked, even though it coulda got me killed.'
28.22: 'Now do what I tell you—eat some food so you got the strength to leave.'
28.23: Saul refused: 'I ain't eatin'.' But his men and the woman kept pushin' him, so he finally sat up.
28.24: The woman had a fat calf at the house, so she hurried up and killed it, made some fresh bread, and cooked a meal.
28.25: She served it to Saul and his men, they ate, and then they left that same night.

29.1: The Philistine army lined up at Aphek, and Israel camped at Jezreel.
29.2: As the Philistine lords marched their troops, David and his men were at the back with Achish.
29.3: The Philistine commanders looked at David and asked Achish, 'Bruh, why are these Hebrews here?!'
29.4: Achish defended David, 'Man, this David—Saul's old guy. He been rollin' with me for years, never caused problems.'
29.5: But the Philistine leaders got mad, 'Send him back! What if he flips on us mid-battle? He tryna win Saul back. Ain't this the same dude they sang about?'
29.6: Achish pulled David aside and said, 'Look, I trust you, but the other lords ain't rockin' with you. You gotta go back.'
29.7: 'I don't want no issues, so go in peace.'
29.8: David was confused, 'What I do wrong? I been loyal. Why can't I fight for you?'
29.9: Achish sighed, 'Man, I see you as an angel from God, but the Philistine leaders don't trust you.'
29.10: 'So get up early, you and your men, and head back at sunrise.'
29.11: David and his crew left early in the morning to return to Philistine land, while the Philistines marched on to Jezreel.

30.1: Three days later, David and his crew pulled up to Ziklag, only to see the Amalekites had run through, raided the south, and torched Ziklag.
30.2: They took all the women and everybody in the city—young and old. They ain't kill nobody, but they kidnapped them all and dipped.
30.3: So when David and his men got back, they saw Ziklag straight up burned down, and their wives, sons, and daughters were gone.
30.4: David and all his people broke down crying, weeping till they ain't have no more tears left.
30.5: Both of David's wives—Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow from Carmel—had been taken too.
30.6: David was real stressed 'cause his own men was talking about stoning him. Everybody was grieving hard over their families being gone. But David found his strength in the Lord his God.
30.7: David told Abiathar, the priest and son of Ahimelech, 'Aye, bring me the ephod.' So Abiathar brought it over to him.
30.8: Then David asked the Lord, 'Should I go after them? Will I catch them?' And the Lord said, 'Go get 'em! You gon' catch up, and you gon' get everything back!'
30.9: So David set out with his 600 men. When they got to the Brook Besor, some of them had to stay back.
30.10: David kept pushing forward with 400 men, while 200 stayed behind 'cause they was too tired to cross the brook.
30.11: They ran into some Egyptian out in the field and brought him to David. They gave him some bread, and he ate. Then they gave him some water.
30.12: They hooked him up with a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. After he ate, he got his strength back, 'cause he ain't had food or water for three days and nights.
30.13: David asked him, 'Who you with? Where you from?' And he said, 'I'm Egyptian, a servant of an Amalekite. My master left me behind three days ago 'cause I got sick.'
30.14: 'We raided the south side of the Cherethites, hit up Judah, and burnt Ziklag down.'
30.15: David asked him, 'Can you take me to them?' The man said, 'Swear to God you won't kill me or send me back to my master, and I'll show you where they at.'
30.16: So he led them down, and there the Amalekites were—chillin', feasting, drinking, and dancing with all the loot they stole from the Philistines and Judah.
30.17: David and his men ran up on them at dusk and fought them all night and all the next day. Ain't nobody get away except 400 young men who hopped on camels and fled.
30.18: David got everything back that the Amalekites took, even his two wives.
30.19: Not a single thing was missing—young or old, sons or daughters, anything they took. David recovered everything.
30.20: Then he took all their flocks and herds. His men gathered them up and said, 'This David's loot now!'
30.21: David got back to the 200 men who had stayed behind at the Brook Besor. They came out to meet him and the rest of the crew. David greeted them warmly.
30.22: But some of the rougher dudes in David's group said, 'They ain't ride out with us, so they don't get none of the loot! Just give 'em back their wives and kids and send them on their way.'
30.23: David said, 'Nah, fam. We not about to do that. The Lord blessed us and kept us safe, letting us take out the enemy that came for us.'
30.24: 'Matter fact, the ones who stayed with the supplies deserve a share just like the ones who fought. Everybody eats!'
30.25: From that day on, that became the rule in Israel—whoever holds it down at home gets the same reward as those on the battlefield.
30.26: When David got back to Ziklag, he sent part of the loot to the elders of Judah—his peoples—saying, 'Here's a gift from the Lord's enemies.'
30.27: He sent some to Bethel, to Ramoth in the South, and to Jattir,
30.29: To Rachal, the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and the cities of the Kenites,
30.31: To Hebron, and all the places where David and his men used to run through.

31.1: The Philistines went to war with Israel, and Israel's army couldn't hang. They turned and ran, but a lot of them got dropped right there on Mount Gilboa.
31.2: The Philistines was on Saul and his sons heavy, and they ended up killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua—Saul's boys.
31.3: The battle got real bad for Saul. Some archers spotted him and lit him up, leaving him badly wounded.
31.4: Saul turned to his armor-bearer and said, 'Man, just finish me off before these uncircumcised fools get to me and do me dirty.' But his armor-bearer was too shook to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
31.5: When the armor-bearer saw Saul was dead, he did the same thing—fell on his own sword and died right there with him.
31.6: So that day, Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men got wiped out together.
31.7: When the Israelites across the valley and beyond the Jordan saw their army retreating and heard that Saul and his sons were dead, they straight up abandoned their towns. The Philistines rolled in and took over.
31.8: The next day, the Philistines came through to loot the dead bodies. That's when they found Saul and his sons lying there on Mount Gilboa.
31.9: They cut off Saul's head, stripped his armor, and sent the news all over Philistine territory—bragging about it in their idol temples and among their people.
31.10: They put his armor in the temple of their goddess Ashtoreth and took his body, fastening it to the wall in Beth Shan.
31.11: When the people of Jabesh-Gilead heard what had happened to Saul,
31.12: Their strongest warriors got up that night, traveled all the way to Beth Shan, and took Saul and his sons' bodies down from the wall. They brought them back to Jabesh and burned them there.
31.13: Then they buried the bones under a tamarisk tree in Jabesh and mourned for seven days, fasting the whole time.
